standard: IEEE 1016-2009 viewpoints (structure from memory; check against the standard before external use)

sections.title: Identification
sections.expect: Project name, owner, version, date, status.

sections.title: Introduction (purpose, scope, definitions)
sections.expect: Purpose, scope and the terms the document defines.

sections.title: Design stakeholders and concerns
sections.expect: Who cares about the design, what they need, and numbered requirements including non-functional ones.

sections.title: Context viewpoint
sections.expect: Context diagram: the system boundary, its users and the external systems.

sections.title: Composition viewpoint
sections.expect: Container diagram: the deployable parts and data stores, what each does, how they communicate (direction, protocol).

sections.title: Logical viewpoint
sections.expect: Logical structure of the main components, if the containers diagram is not enough.

sections.title: Dependency viewpoint
sections.expect: Technologies and third-party services used, each checked against the radar or backed by an ADR.

sections.title: Information viewpoint
sections.expect: Data model, plus data class, residency and retention for every data flow.

sections.title: Patterns use viewpoint
sections.expect: Named design patterns used and where.

sections.title: Interface viewpoint
sections.expect: Every interface: contract, version, protocol, who calls whom, how callers are identified.

sections.title: Structure viewpoint
sections.expect: How the code or deployment units are organised.

sections.title: Interaction viewpoint
sections.expect: Sequence diagrams for the key flows.

sections.title: State dynamics viewpoint
sections.expect: State diagram for any long-running process, with one named owner of its status, timers and retries.

sections.title: Algorithm viewpoint
sections.expect: Non-trivial decision logic, model use or scoring, if any.

sections.title: Resource viewpoint (deployment)
sections.expect: Deployment diagram: where each container runs (account or subscription, region, network zone or cluster), trust and network boundaries, managed services.

sections.title: Design overlays (security, identity, observability)
sections.expect: Security, identity and observability design, including tracing and audit.

sections.title: Design rationale
sections.expect: Why each significant technology or pattern was chosen: an ADR or a stated reason, with alternatives and the cost of moving.

sections.title: ARB conformance and reuse
sections.expect: Which catalogue building blocks are reused, what is contributed back, and any exceptions.

sections.title: Open issues
sections.expect: Open design questions, each with an owner and a date. Nothing that blocks the design may stay open.
